P1.evidence: Notes were genuinely read back and with specifics: 'some of the stuff you kind of shared last time, I got some basic notes... I remember you saying like 63 now, it's been a little bit more difficult to trim fat and gain muscle.' He also used the application later — 'I saw in your application, you're wanting to add 20 to 30 pounds to your lifts.' But no frame was set at all on this call, four-part or otherwise, and no frame agreement was sought. Instead of an open question he offered a recap for confirmation and moved straight to 'What's the motivation behind getting into shape like this right now?' The rep re-ran a full baseline on this call, so treating it as a fresh discovery without re-framing it is a genuine miss rather than a continuation.

P2.evidence: Age, height and weight asked directly. Training week walked through exercise by exercise. Diet asked. Work asked along with the sitting question, and followed with 'Have you noticed any like mobility issues at all with work?' Results from current training probed twice — 'How are we feeling about the physique as a whole right now?' and 'What do you think has been missing for you?' Injuries asked and followed up: 'Any major injuries?' then 'Any issues with working out with the shoulders at all?' The rep also asked an unscripted but useful health question, 'Are you on TRT at all, Ken?', which opened the clomiphene disclosure. Hereditary conditions were never asked, sleep was never asked and energy was never asked.

P3.evidence: The one-thing question ran and was pushed for more: 'what would like the ideal physique be?... What else? Anything else?' The bridge was the best moment of the phase and properly confrontational: 'most guys in their 60s is just like, okay dude, things are good... You already have the wife, you got the kid, you got the grandkids... what's the drive behind this, man? And I know part of it is wife and kids, but I mean, they'll love you either way.' That produced the identity answer — 'I'm not going to have a dad bod... my belly shows through my shirt, it just pisses me off' — and later 'we love getting it on. So I'm going to stay in shape as long as I can to please her.' The rep then went sideways into how the couple met and how the grandson came about, and never returned. No reflect-back was ever attempted, nothing was asked about a physical thing he cannot do, and the ten-pull-up goal he volunteered was never acknowledged.

P4.evidence: This prospect has not failed in the usual sense — he has trained consistently for two years — so the classic past-attempts sequence has less to bite on, but the rep still under-ran it. 'What do you think has been missing for you?' landed the key admission: 'having a routine that I'm comfortable with, that it's making a difference. Sometimes I just feel like I'm going through the motions.' The standout probe was on mobility: 'What's had you avoid mobility up to this point?' — 'I guess I don't see as much bang for my buck.' That is a real root cause and the rep answered it with an anecdote instead of using it. Nothing was asked about what he has tried and abandoned over a lifetime of training.

P5.evidence: Absent entirely. No two-year question, no settling question, no why-not, no line in the sand. The nearest thing was 'What actually shifted for you or what happened where it became more of a priority all of a sudden?', which is a trigger question rather than a consequence frame. For a 63-year-old with two shoulder replacements, a deferred knee surgery and an explicit fear of losing muscle to age, the cost-of-inaction material was sitting in plain view and was never asked for. This is the fifth consecutive call in the batch where P5 is absent or vestigial.

P6.evidence: Both commitment reads were soft and the rep devalued the second one himself, twice: 'This is going to be an obvious answer, but Trevor always wants me to ask it' and then 'kind of an obvious question, but again, Trevor always has me ask it.' The belief question got a deferential non-answer that was treated as a yes: 'do you feel like that's everything that you need to get into like the incredible shape that we talked about?' — 'You know better than I do, Michael, but I think that could work.' That is not a clear YES and the script says do not proceed without one. The consequence arrived within a minute of the price: 'I'm going to think about it.'

P11.evidence: Payment collected live and confirmed — 'Okay, that went through perfect then' — and the onboarding call booked on the call for 5:15pm Central the next day, which the prospect confirmed he could see in his inbox. Step 3 failed: the agreement never arrived. The prospect checked his inbox and his spam and then a second email account, and reported 'Not through yet', 'Yeah, don't see anything' and 'All I see is the scheduled meeting.' Nothing was signed on the call and the rep deferred it to a text he would send later. Step 4 partly failed with it, because the Skool and onboarding links were described as flowing from the agreement that never fired; the onboarding questionnaire was never mentioned at all. The rep closed the call with 'I got to hop on one more call here', and the back-to-back booking is visibly why the last two steps were left open.

objection_plays.detail: 'I'm going to think about it. Obviously, I'm all in on doing it, but that's 6K for six months.' The rep ran the opening isolation well — 'Finances aside though, do you feel like ultimately everything we covered... checks all the boxes for you and it can get you to where you want to be?' — and then a strong unscripted probe, 'What's the last one you did?', which surfaced a $6,000 peptide purchase and a $20,000 vacation club and effectively removed affordability from the table. He never ran 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', never used 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', and never closed with 'are you sure? Nothing else keeping you from being 100% in.' He abandoned the play and switched to a reduced-price entry instead.

Money was raised but the rep diagnosed it correctly and fast: 'it really seems not so much like a matter of us not having the investments, more just a kind of a value, like uncertainty kind of thing at this point.' The prospect confirmed it. Because capacity was proven, skipping the six financial-picture questions was the right judgement here rather than a failure — this is the one call in the batch where not running them was correct. What is missing is the other half: no payment plan was ever structured, and the discount request was correctly refused and then functionally granted five minutes later in the form of a $1,200 entry tier.

Real and specific fear, stated twice: 'I'm just starting out and I don't want to blow a shoulder out' and the direct meniscus question. The rep answered with product mechanics and reassurance — light starting weights, video form checks, mobility, and 'it becomes harder and harder to get injured over time' — rather than the scripted moves. It resolved the objection commercially, but it resolved it by asserting safety to a man with two prosthetic shoulders and a torn meniscus, which is flagged separately. None of the OE language ran: no certainty frame, no bridge, no 'how will you know if you never actually try'.

Script gap that this rep solved on the fly and the playbook should capture. The objection was not price and not a cheaper competitor — it was the prospect himself as the free alternative: 'can I get there on my own and my own discipline?' The rep conceded the point rather than fighting it, then converted the prospect's own professional pricing logic into the answer: 'to most people, four grand, five grand a day, that's going to be absolutely crazy, but to a business owner who understands the value of results, not time, it's going to be well worth the investment... even if he just saves you a day of time over the next six months, you're basically paying for it right then and there.' The prospect capitulated openly — 'I never should have told you my hourly rate, Michael' and 'The logic adds up.' This is the single most effective improvised move in the batch and there is nothing like it in the script.

notes: The deal was won on one excellent improvised move — mirroring the prospect's own day rate back at him — and the process around it was thin: no frame, no consequence frame at all, and a commitment check the rep verbally discounted twice before asking it, which produced a soft yes that folded on contact with the price. He then bought the objection off with a $1,200 entry tier rather than finishing OA. Coach the sequence and the stop conditions, not the persuasion. Separately, P11 needs a hard rule: back-to-back bookings meant a paying client left the call with no signed agreement and no confirmed onboarding materials.
